newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gen.des Eaux to start fixed phone service in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Gen.des Eaux to start fixed phone service in 1998.

text.p: The executive chairman of Compagnie Generale des Eaux said in a newspaper interview on Sunday that the group's new fixed-line telephone service will be available throughout France at the start of 1998.
"As of January 1, 1998, each Frenchman will be able to call everywhere in the world through Generale des Eaux even from a fixed-line phone," Jean-Marie Messier told Le Journal du Dimanche.
Messier explained that Generale des Eaux aimed to have a share of 20 percent of the French fixed-line telephone market within five years and 10 percent of the market for business services.

The group's Cegetel unit said in November it had received permission from French authorities to try out the fixed-phone network in the southern city of Nice ahead of the liberalisaton of the market in 1998.
Cegetel will offer residential telecom services from the start of 1997 in Nice.
The new fixed-line phone network will compete with that of state-owned France Telecom.
Competition should drive down the prices of fixed-line communications by some 10 percent each year, Messier predicted.
In mobile telecommunications, Generale des Eaux already competes with France Telecom with its SFR unit.
Messier said SFR expects to have one million customers by February 1997, having added 110,000 new customers in December.
